songs.name: And We Bid You Good Night

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Fillmore set with stellar Dark Star, Alligator>Caution jam
ai_show_review.blurb: The second set delivers a blazing Alligator > Caution sequence, a soaring Dark Star and an inspired Other One > New Potato run. Jerry’s lead work is relentless while Phil supplies aggressive, funky bass throughout. The recording captures the entire performance with clear stereo matrix sound despite some mono sections in the first set.
ai_show_review.review: August 22, 1968 at Fillmore West finds the Dead firing on all cylinders. After a rough opening that leans on a mono radio feed for Saint Stephen and The Eleven, the band quickly gains momentum, driving through Death Don't Have No Mercy into a rousing Turn On Your Lovelight. The second set is where the night truly shines: Dark Star unfolds with Jerry’s crystal‑clear leads and Phil’s zooming bass, segues into a hypnotic Cryptical Envelopment sandwich, then erupts into an electrifying Other One > New Potato stretch. The Alligator > Caution jam builds to a peak that feels both propulsive and spontaneous, capped off by a standout Feedback finale before the band bids good night. Across all three recordings the performance is consistently high‑energy, with tight interplay, daring improvisation, and one of Bill’s most memorable drum solos captured in surprisingly clear stereo.

best_recording.reason: Full‑show matrix capture with clear stereo on the second set and balanced mix, preserving every jam while covering the entire performance.

key_highlights: Alligator > Caution sequence drives the second set with relentless momentum
Dark Star showcases soaring guitar lines and aggressive bass duels
Other One > New Potato delivers a tight, exploratory jam
Bill Kreutzmann’s drum solo stands out as one of the era’s best

band_performance.Jerry: Endless runs and perfect ’68‑tone guitar; leads Dark Star and Alligator>Caution with relentless intensity.
band_performance.Phil: Aggressive, funky bass that duels with Jerry in The Eleven and drives the high‑energy jams, especially New Potato.
band_performance.Pigpen: Organ adds perfect texture on Death Don't Have No Mercy; provides solid keyboard foundation throughout the jams.
band_performance.Billy: Drums go nuts on the Alligator drum solo and maintain a propulsive groove across the second‑set improvisations.
